match_note: The core figures, model and claims match arXiv v1. These include the Fig. 3 many-body energy and current-component panels with 011→111 and 100→110 labels, W = 50 meV, the 2^3 = 8 state reduction, the Γ = 10–20 meV vs PME weak-coupling caveat, and the hexamer. The text, however, differs in places. The peer-review title ('Non-Equilibrium Correlated Electron Dynamics...') differs from v1 ('Negative differential conductance...'). Several sentences R3 quotes from page 2 ('we directly visualize discharging processes and characteristic Coulomb ring patterns...', '(dis)charging rings and conductance discontinuities do not correspond to a change in the total charge...') do not appear verbatim in v1. The rebuttal mentions Extended Data Figures and a transfer from Nature Physics, whereas v1 uses Supplementary Figs. S1–S14. The reviewed manuscript is therefore likely a reworded version of v1 with essentially the same science; whether it is the identical version is unclear.

concerns.quote: I wonder why the background in section 3 with one electron on the cluster has three distinct areas (010, 010, 100) rather than the 010 and 001 being at the same energy?
concerns.summary: The coloured background regions in Fig. 3a are confusing; it is unclear whether they show ground states and why degenerate states appear as separate areas.

concerns.quote: Are the colored contributions relative contributions or some absolute values? The current seems to vary already along the red molecule. Why? Where does the exponential dependence enter
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the current components in Fig. 3b are absolute or relative, why the current varies over the red molecule, and where the exponential tip-distance dependence shows up.

concerns.quote: The description of figures and their meaning is minimal in the paper. More details should be presented in the revised version.
concerns.summary: The discussion of the figures, especially the complex Fig. 3a and 3b, is too brief to follow.

concerns.quote: They may want to stress that the molecules are charged in their ground state as can be deduced from the YSR spectra already at this point, possibly even including the spectra in the main manuscript.
concerns.summary: The paper should establish early, using the YSR spectra (possibly shown in the main text), that the molecules are charged in the ground state, which justifies calling the rings discharging.

concerns.quote: They may also want to comment on the origin of the splitting of the YSR states.
concerns.summary: The main text should explain the origin of the observed YSR peak splitting.

concerns.quote: it would help to mention highly relevant related work on quantum dot trimers (triple quantum dots)... the underlying theoretical model is basically the same.
concerns.summary: Relevant prior work on triangular triple quantum dots, which show correlation-induced collective states and ground-state switching, should be cited.

concerns.quote: quantum interference effects are also important for interacting systems -- but one must now think about many-body quantum interference in Fock space... I suggest placing the current work in the proper context.
concerns.summary: The work should be placed in the context of many-body quantum interference between Dyson-orbital transition amplitudes, not just charge rearrangement.

concerns.quote: how/why is a single-orbital approximation appropriate? ... The approximation appears to be justified post hoc by comparison with experiment, but what is the physical reason for this drastic simplification?
concerns.summary: Representing each molecule by a single Anderson orbital lacks physical justification beyond agreement with experiment.

concerns.quote: Why is a superconducting substrate used, and what role does it play here? It would seem to me that this could complicate transport signatures significantly
concerns.summary: The choice and role of a superconducting substrate is unexplained and could complicate the transport signatures.

concerns.quote: For the NRG studies, more details of the implementation and calculations performed must be provided... All model and NRG parameters as well as further corroborating data should be provided.
concerns.summary: NRG implementation details, the full parameter set and corroborating data are insufficient for reproducibility.

concerns.quote: what is the justification for the transport formulae used? Why not use Landauer-Buttiker or Meir-Wingreen for a more rigorous description?
concerns.summary: The transport formulae in the SI are not justified against more rigorous Landauer-Büttiker or Meir-Wingreen approaches.

concerns.quote: Given the off-diagonal substrate hybridization terms, do we end up with a complicated multi-channel Kondo model? ... Why are there no off-diagonal hybridization terms with the tip?
concerns.summary: The form of the hybridization matrix needs justification: whether the model is single-channel (a common bath orbital) or multichannel, and why tip off-diagonal terms are omitted.

concerns.quote: how is the weak-coupling approximation justified and why does it work so well? ... we are told that Gamma>10T and so this is really not the sequential tunnelling regime.
concerns.summary: The Markovian weak-coupling PME is questionable at low temperature with Γ well above T, and the definition and physical meaning of Γ are unclear.

concerns.quote: I do not really understand the reduction to 2^3=8 states. Precluding double occupancy leaves 3 states on each SOMO so I would have thought this is 3^3=27 states
concerns.summary: The Hilbert-space reduction to 8 states appears inconsistent, since excluding double occupancy leaves 27 spinful states, and the tractability argument is mis-framed.

concerns.quote: the substrate is superconducting and therefore at low T can only accept or release cooper pairs... Another possibility is that the actual quantum N=2e state is a superposition
concerns.summary: Intra-cluster charge reorganization via single-electron substrate tunnelling is questionable on a superconductor; pair tunnelling or coherent superpositions of configurations may be the real mechanism.

concerns.quote: it seems that the trimer does not gain or loss charge in the whole process. If this is the case, the author shall not use charging/discharging, which confuses the readers.
concerns.summary: Calling features 'charging/discharging' is misleading when the total cluster charge is conserved.

concerns.quote: Experimentally, these charge states can be confirmed using Kelvin parabolas showing the LCPD using nc-AFM. To unambiguously verify the proposed mechanism, such measurements are essential.
concerns.summary: The proposed cluster charge states (−2e, −1e) should be verified independently by nc-AFM Kelvin parabola/LCPD measurements.

concerns.quote: Figure 3b shows at the left side the charge is 2 as labelled with "011", while at the right side the charge is 1 as labelled with "001". The labels are confusing. Also, Fig. 3b shows 011->111
concerns.summary: The state labels in Fig. 3b appear inconsistent with the total charges marked in Fig. 3d, and the 011→111 process is not discussed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: It is not clear for the reviewer how the bias voltage of the STM junction is treated in the modelling... a concise presentation of the Hamiltonian and/or schematic configuration of the system shall be presented in the main text.
concerns.summary: The treatment of the bias voltage in the model is unclear, and a concise Hamiltonian or schematic should be given in the main text.

first_round.quote: I recommend publication of this paper in Nature Communications, but would like to request some more detailed descriptions as commented below
This work is entirely suited for publication in Nature Communications (or Nature Physics for that matter). I have the following questions and suggestions to improve the manuscript and analysis
Experimentally, these charge states can be confirmed using Kelvin parabolas showing the LCPD using nc-AFM. To unambiguously verify the proposed mechanism, such measurements are essential.

recommendations.note: Recommendations are taken from Version 0, the first round in this file. The authors' list of changes says the manuscript was transferred from Nature Physics, so any earlier Nature Physics review round is not included here. No referee used the scale terms, so all three levels are inferred. R1 and R2 support publication and ask mainly for clarifications, context and added details, so they are rated minor revision. R3 gives no overall verdict but calls new nc-AFM/Kelvin parabola measurements 'essential' and asks for substantially expanded discussion, so they are rated major revision. No referee co-signed another's report. All three recommended acceptance in Version 1.
recommendations.label: contested
